originalGroup.material:
The orange cap

Jack has an orange cap. On Saturday, he goes to the park with his sister Mia. Jack rides his bike, and Mia walks beside him. They take some bread and two bottles of water.

Jack puts his cap on a bench when they stop to eat. After lunch, he runs to the swings. Mia sees the cap and puts it in her bag.

When they go home, Jack asks, "Where's my cap?" Mia opens her bag. "Here it is!" she says. Jack smiles and puts it on.

originalGroup.material:
A snack in the garden

It is Sunday afternoon. Emma and her dad are in the garden. Dad reads a book under a tree. Emma draws a picture of their house.

At three o'clock, Mum brings a plate of apples and pears. Emma takes a pear. Dad takes an apple. Their dog Pip sits beside the table, but he does not eat the fruit.

Then it starts to rain. They take the book and picture into the house. Pip runs in too. Emma puts her picture on the kitchen wall. She wants Grandma to see it on Monday.

originalGroup.material:
Calling the toy museum

Woman: Toy Museum. Can I help you?
Ben: Hello. I'd like to visit with my dad tomorrow. Are you open on Wednesday?
Woman: Yes. We open at ten and close at five.
Ben: Can we see the old trains?
Woman: Yes. They are in Room 2, upstairs. The dolls are downstairs.
Ben: Is there a toy-making class?
Woman: There is one at eleven. It takes an hour. Children over seven can join it.
Ben: I'm nine. Do I need to bring anything?
Woman: No. We have the paper and glue here. Please book a place before you come.
Ben: How do I book?
Woman: Your dad can use our website. The class is four pounds for each child. He can watch for free.
Ben: Can we eat lunch there?
Woman: You can use the picnic tables outside. Food is not allowed in the rooms.
Ben: Thank you. I'll tell my dad.

originalGroup.material:
A call about the beans

Grandpa: Hello, Lucy. How are your plants?
Lucy: Two are tall, but the third is still small.
Grandpa: Where do you keep the pots?
Lucy: On my desk. The tall plants are beside the window. The small one is behind my big book box.
Grandpa: Can it get much light there?
Lucy: No. The box is in the way.
Grandpa: Move the box first. Then you can put all three pots near the window.
Lucy: Shall I give the small plant lots of water?
Grandpa: Check the soil. If it is wet, don't add more now.
Lucy: It's wet today. I'll wait.
Grandpa: Good. Take a photograph every Friday. Then you can see how the plants change.
Lucy: Will you visit this weekend?
Grandpa: On Sunday morning, after breakfast.
Lucy: Great! I'll show you my photographs.

originalGroup.sourceNotice: 2026-10-24新题批次 b023；原创候选，非高考真题；自审及程序检查，不声称独立教师或学生稳定性验证。
originalGroup.material:
Frog's audience

In a valley of talking animals, Frog loved singing. One afternoon, he practised beside a rocky hill. When he sang a long note, the same note came back to him.

"Someone likes my song!" he thought. He sang louder, and the returning sound grew louder too. Frog ran to Owl and announced that he had a hidden audience inside the hill.

Owl came to listen. Instead of singing, she called, "Good afternoon!" The words came back. Frog looked surprised.

"The rock is returning the sound," Owl explained. "It is an echo, not another singer."

Frog felt foolish. He wanted to leave, but Owl asked him to sing once more. This time, he listened to the pause before the note returned. Soon he made a short song with spaces in it, letting the echo answer each line.

That evening, Frog invited his friends to the hill. He explained the echo before he began. They enjoyed the song, and when it ended, they really did clap. Frog was pleased with the applause, but he was also glad he had learned what the first sound meant.

originalGroup.material:
Bear's market bell

In a town of talking animals, Bear sold vegetables at the market. He bought a bright bell and rang it whenever he wanted customers to look at his stall.

At first, everyone turned. Bear rang the bell for fresh carrots, then for a clean table, then because he liked its sound. Soon the other sellers stopped looking up. Some customers moved to the quieter end of the market.

One morning, Bear received the first strawberries of the season. He rang his bell, but Rabbit walked past without noticing. Bear was puzzled. He had expected his best fruit to bring the most attention.

Rabbit explained, "Your bell used to tell us something new. Now we hear it all the time. We don't know when it matters."

Bear put the bell under the table. He wrote clear prices on a board and spoke to customers who came near. For a week, he did not ring it once.

On the following Saturday, he held a short strawberry-tasting event. He rang the bell once, then explained the invitation. People turned and listened. Bear kept the bell, but he no longer used it simply to fill the air.

originalGroup.material:
Four books for the reading club

Choose one book for the reading club's holiday project. Read it during the holiday, then bring a one-page response on the first Friday of next term. You may borrow a copy from the school library.

Book | Length | Main subject | Special feature
The Moon Post Office | 96 pages | A girl delivers letters in an imaginary town | Short chapters and black-and-white drawings
Bridge for an Ant | 72 pages | Talking insects solve a problem together | A map at the beginning
The Storm Piano | 144 pages | A boy learns an old family song | A small glossary of music words
The Hidden Watch | 128 pages | Two friends investigate a missing object | Clues shown in pictures as well as words

You may write about a character, draw an important scene with an explanation, or compare two parts of your chosen story. Do not copy a review from the internet. The response should show your own reading.

The library has two copies of each book. Reservations open on Monday. Books must be returned by the second Wednesday of next term. There is no requirement to choose the longest book, and responses will not be judged by how many pages you have read.

You may write about a character, draw an important scene with an explanation, or compare two parts of your chosen story. Do not copy a review from the internet. The response should show your own reading.

The library has two copies of each book. Reservations open on Monday. Books must be returned by the second Wednesday of next term. There is no requirement to choose the longest book, and responses will not be judged by how many pages you have read.

originalGroup.sourceNotice: 2026-10-24新题批次 b023；原创候选，非高考真题；自审及程序检查，不声称独立教师或学生稳定性验证。
originalGroup.material:
Four holiday visits

The school travel club has arranged four visits during the holiday. Each student may book one visit. Fees include transport and entry. Bring your own lunch unless the table says lunch is included.

Visit | Day | Leaving/returning | Fee | Notes
Coastal Bird Centre | Tuesday | 8:30/16:00 | 12 pounds | Outdoor walk; bring binoculars if you have them
Town Print Museum | Wednesday | 9:00/15:00 | 10 pounds | Indoor printmaking activity; wear old clothes
Hill Farm | Thursday | 8:00/17:00 | 15 pounds | Lunch included; tell us about food allergies
Railway Workshop | Friday | 9:30/15:30 | 11 pounds | Closed shoes required; no sandals

Meet at the school gate fifteen minutes before departure. A teacher will travel with every group. Book through the school office by next Monday, with a parent's permission.

If strong winds make the coastal walk unsafe, that visit will be postponed and families will receive a message by 18:00 on Monday. The other visits are not affected by that decision. Students who do not own binoculars may still join the bird-centre visit. Do not buy a pair just for the trip.
